data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism is internally contradictory. It states that acting on the best-tested theory is 'the only rational way to pursue truth,' yet simultaneously defines corroboration as 'a report card of past critical efforts rather than a predictor of future success.' If corroboration is explicitly not a predictor of future success, then preferring corroborated theories has no warranted connection to the goal of pursuing truth — the methodological rule would be a mere convention, not a rationally truth-directed strategy. The target thus claims 'procedural rationality' but the procedure it describes lacks any defensible link to truth-seeking, since by its own admission past test-survival tells us nothing about whether the theory will hold going forward. This smuggles in the very problem it claims to solve: without some minimal assumption that surviving severe tests is relevant to future performance, calling the preference 'rational' as a truth-pursuing strategy is unsupported, and the claim that it is 'the only rational way' is an overreach.
